storyboard.premise: Node Foyer claims to read every product's own public files, live, on every sweep, and never invent a state.
storyboard.question: Does the grid actually reflect what each product currently serves, and does the apparatus behind every colour hold a real probe?
storyboard.axis: verified (two layers agree) vs reachable-only (answered, nothing to compare) vs unknown (never answered)
storyboard.conflict: a fixture adapter (__fixture_dead) wired to a URL that always fails, run on every sweep so the honest-failure path is exercised, not assumed
storyboard.evidence: hover apparatus: probe URL, HTTP status, fetch time, remote Date header, sha256, the per-layer match line, and the stated reason
storyboard.verdict: 22 cards, one honest state each; the Foyer's own card is verified on both its frontend and backend layers; the dead fixture stays UNKNOWN with its tried URL on screen
storyboard.exit: trust the pill colour because the apparatus behind it is inspectable on this same screen, not because the pill says so

frames.caption: For a release lead who has to trust a status board without reading anyone's source code: this board checks the ten hosted products' own live pages every half hour and shows exactly what came back. Nobody typed these results in by hand.
Twenty-two products are tracked here, each with its own honest badge. The ten that are hosted get checked the exact same way; the rest say so with a registry-only badge.

Green means verified. For this product both the website people see and the service behind it were checked on the last sweep, and both reported the same version. Amber means it answered, but there was nothing to compare against.
This green badge has held steady for 21 checks in a row, back to back — not just one lucky moment.
Hovering shows the receipt behind the badge: the exact address it checked, when it checked, and a short fingerprint of what came back, so anyone can double-check it themselves.
One product here is deliberately broken on purpose, to prove the checker doesn't fake results: it always shows unknown, and shows the exact address it tried and failed to reach.
This board even checks itself. Verified means that after a new version of this board goes live, it reads its own page back and confirms the version numbers match — that's what turns this badge green.
